title: task status-flow's manifest `fields` omits closedStatus and resolutions, which the command emits (QCLI-461 class)
description:
Found while landing QCLI-325 (review seq 8416) and reported then: task status-flow's advertised manifest `fields` is a CURATED SUBSET, not the complete key set -- the same under-declaration class QCLI-461 closed for task list, task view and search.

MEASURED. src/application/command-contract.ts declares fields [statuses, terminalStatuses, pausedStatus, pausedStatusConfigurable], while src/cli/commands/task/index.ts emits `closedStatus` and `resolutions` too whenever a closed status is configured. Nothing in-repo enforces status-flow's declared-versus-emitted set: QCLI-461's payload-subset-of-declared assertion runs over task view, task list and search only, and the adapter boundary comparison (test/contract/tracker/lore-adapter-boundary.test.ts) skips status-flow because ADAPTER_REQUIRED_MANIFEST_COMMANDS carries no `fields` key for it -- which is why bun run check passes with the two keys undeclared.

SAME CLASS AS QCLI-461 (which completed task list/view/search and deliberately left this surface alone). The fix is to declare the complete emitted key set for task status-flow, updating the manifest and its three mirrors together, and to extend the declared-versus-emitted assertion to cover it. Filed by the quest-cli worker at team-lead instruction -- the team-lead explicitly asked for this one; UNSTAMPED.

acceptanceCriteria.text: task status-flow's manifest `fields` contains every top-level key the command emits (closedStatus and resolutions included), updated in the manifest and its mirrors, and an assertion covers the emitted-subset-of-declared direction for it
